column2: re-mounting the memory controller after using it is

column1: very likely to hang.
The cgroup core assumes that any remaining references after deleting a
cgroup are temporary in nature
the above-mentioned commit has left-over page cache pin its css until
it is reclaimed naturally.  That being said
kernel memory have been doing the same indefinite pinning forever
bug is just more likely to trigger with left-over page cache.
Reparenting kernel memory is highly impractical
the cgroup assumptions to reflect this: once a controller has been
mounted and used
column2: it has internal state that is independent from mount

column1: and cgroup lifetime.  It can be unmounted and remounted
be reconfigured during subsequent mounts.
Don't offline the controller root as long as there are any children
dead or alive.  A remount will no longer wait for these old references
to drain
column2: it will simply mount the persistent controller state again.
